text:
charlie: Heads-up — HarborPay prod showing elevated tail latency on /v1/generate since ~08:40 UTC. Customer reported timeouts, support flagged SLA risk. Can eng-platform own triage + a short-term mitigation plan?
laura: Thanks. Do we know if it's a model-serving issue or infra (autoscaler/queue) related? Any error spikes in logs?
support-bot: HarborPay ticket #HP-412: repeated 504s from our gateway, affect ~3% of requests, started after a config push at 08:37. Customer is asking for ETA on fix.
sanjay: I looked at the autoscaler charts — sudden drop in worker availability in us-west-2 between 08:36–08:38, pods restarted. Could be kernel OOM on a node class that runs dedicated pools. Taking ownership to correlate with infra team.
dmitri: I pulled the runtime logs, seeing repeated kv-cache OOMs around the same time. Example excerpt:```ERROR runtime: KVCache eviction failed: out of memory``` Not sure if it's caused by model change or batch size spike.
mika: @sanjay @dmitri, can we get a quick repro? If it's kv-cache OOM, temporary mitigation is to disable prefix caching for HarborPay route and drop max_batch_tokens. That reduces throughput but avoids OOM.
charlie: Agreed. We need two actions: 1) short-term mitigation to restore SLA (within ~30m), 2) postmortem/root cause and a rollout guard. Who can implement the workaround and who will own postmortem?
sanjay: I'll coordinate with infra to confirm node health and restart strategy. I can apply a routing override to point HarborPay to smaller batch profile and disable prefix cache for the route. ETA 20–30m.
laura: I'll own the postmortem and follow-up on rollout guard (add alert for config pushes that change caching params). Adding code-review pings for the guard change.
dmitri: I'll open a quick PR for a runtime fallback that detects kv-cache oom and auto-switches to safe mode. It's not perfect but buys time. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/487 — requesting review from @mika and @sanjay.
mika: Reviewing now, pinging @laura for testing instructions. Also suggest adding a small metric for 'fallback_switches' so we can correlate.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 HarborPay high tail latency. Severity: S2. Pager escalation set to on-call infra if mitigation fails in 15m.
deploy-bot: Canary config override queued for HarborPay-route in us-west-2. Planned at 09:05 UTC. If rollout succeeds, will promote to all regions.
support-bot: Customer update drafted: "We've identified a serving instability and applied an immediate mitigation. We'll provide ETA for a permanent fix within 4 hours." Waiting for approval.
charlie: Summarizing owners: short-term config override -> @sanjay (apply + verify), runtime safe-mode PR -> @dmitri (owner), postmortem & rollout guard -> @laura, reviews/testing -> @mika. Support message approved.
laura: I'll schedule a postmortem call at 13:00 UTC and collect logs/metrics before then. Please drop any relevant screenshots or traces in this thread.
sanjay: Override applied at 09:07 UTC to HarborPay-route (batch_size=8, prefix_cache=false). Initial metrics show error rate dropping. Monitoring for 15m to confirm. :thumbsup:
charlie: Thanks all. If error rate doesn't drop to <0.5% in 30m we escalate to S1 with infra on pager.
mika: Quick note for reviews — I'll prioritize the runtime PR this sprint. If we need a hotfix, mark it with label "hotfix/urgent".
charlie: Closing loop: please update thread when you have verification or if you hit blockers. Good work moving fast. :rocket:
